The correct evaluation uses the substitution \(y=g(x)=x^{7}+6x^{5}+3x^{3}+1\). Since \(g\) is strictly increasing, \(f(y)=9g^{-1}(y)+5\). Hence  

\[
\int_{-9}^{11} f(y)\,dy=\int_{-1}^{1} (9t+5)\,g'(t)\,dt
      =\int_{-1}^{1}\!\bigl(63t^{7}+270t^{5}+81t^{3}+35t^{6}+150t^{4}+45t^{2}\bigr)dt .
\]

All odd‑power terms integrate to zero over \([-1,1]\). The remaining even terms give  

\[
\int_{-1}^{1}\!(35t^{6}+150t^{4}+45t^{2})dt
   =\Bigl[5t^{7}+30t^{5}+15t^{3}\Bigr]_{-1}^{1}
   =\bigl(5+30+15\bigr)-\bigl(-5-30-15\bigr)=100 .
\]

Thus  

\[
\boxed{ \displaystyle \int_{-9}^{11} f(x)\,dx = 100 }.
\]

The proposed answer \(\frac{265}{4}=66.25\) is not correct.
